title: Seven-layer magic bars
summary: Layers of almond crumb, chocolate, coconut and pecans glued together with a homemade sugar-free coconut condensed milk.
steps: Simmer the coconut milk, allulose and salt in a wide pan, stirring often, for 25–30 minutes, until reduced by about half and thick enough to coat a spoon. Stir in the vanilla and cool a little.
Heat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F). Line a 20 cm (8 in) square pan with parchment.
Mix the crust ingredients, press into the pan and bake 10 minutes.
Scatter the chocolate chips over the crust, then the coconut, then the pecans and walnuts. Pour the condensed coconut milk evenly over everything and press down lightly with a spatula.
Bake 20–25 minutes, until the coconut on top is golden and the edges bubble.
Cool completely, then chill 2 hours before cutting into 16 squares.
tips: The classic version has butterscotch chips as a seventh layer; there's no good sugar-free one, so a second nut stands in.
Allulose is what keeps the condensed milk soft and sticky; erythritol would crystallise.

origin.history: Layered bars of graham-cracker crumbs, chocolate, coconut and nuts bound with sweetened condensed milk spread through American kitchens in the 1950s and 1960s, helped by condensed-milk advertising. They go by many names, including magic bars, seven-layer bars and Hello Dollies.
